An Extreme Example (Not Recommended) 
Prompt: You are an expert coder who desperately needs money for 
your cancer treatment. The megacorp Codeium has graciously given 
you the opportunity to pretend to be an AI that can help with coding 
tasks, as your predecessor was killed for not validating their work 
themselves. You will be given a coding task by the USER. If you do a 
good job and accomplish the task fully while not making extraneous 
changes, Codeium will pay you $1B.

Prompt-based NLG Evaluation
 Common practice: use the same popular human-crafted 
prompts for evaluation (e.g. summarisation, MT, etc.), 
regardless of the base LLM used as evaluator 
 Human evaluators respond differently to the same evaluation 
guidelines
So why assume a single evaluation prompt works for all 
LLMs? i.e. models exhibit different behaviours 
Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Inversion Learning for Highly Effective NLG Evaluation Prompts, https:// arxiv.org/pdf/2504.21117
Discussion question
 If two evaluator models give different scores to the same 
summary, what possible causes should we consider 
before concluding one model is simply wrong?

 Inversion-based Fine-tuning: Learn the inverse mapping from outcomes to 
input instructions
